interview.q: What is the main axis in flexbox?
interview.answer: The primary direction along which flex items are laid out, controlled by flex-direction.
The axis perpendicular to the main axis, used for alignment with align-items and align-content.
It lays items left to right in a horizontal main axis.
It lays items top to bottom in a vertical main axis.
It controls whether items wrap to a new line when they exceed the container width.
It places the first item at the start, the last at the end, and distributes equal space between the rest.

interview.q: What is the difference between space-around and space-evenly?
interview.answer: space-around gives half-size gaps at the edges; space-evenly gives equal gaps everywhere including edges.
It centres items along the cross axis within their line.
It overrides align-items for a single flex item.
It defines how much a flex item grows relative to others when free space is available.
It defines how much a flex item shrinks relative to others when space is tight.

interview.q: How does flex-basis differ from width in a flex item?
interview.answer: flex-basis is the starting size before flex distribution and can be overridden by flex-grow; width is a fixed size.
It sets flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 1 and flex-basis: 0%, making items share space equally.
Because flex-basis: 0 ignores content size, so long content can overflow unless min-width is handled.

interview.q: What is min-width: 0 used for in flexbox?
interview.answer: It lets a flex item shrink below its content size, preventing overflow in a row.
It sets flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 1 and flex-basis: auto, so items grow but start from their content size.
It sets flex-grow: 0, flex-shrink: 0 and flex-basis: auto, making the item inflexible.
It aligns wrapped lines along the cross axis in a multi-line flex container.

interview.q: What is the difference between align-items and align-content?
interview.answer: align-items aligns items within a line; align-content aligns the lines themselves when wrapping.
It changes the visual order of a flex item without changing the DOM order.

interview.q: Why is order risky for accessibility?
interview.answer: Screen readers and tab order follow the DOM, not the visual order, so mismatches confuse users.
It adds space between flex items without adding margins to the edges.
It lays items right to left while keeping the main axis horizontal.
It lays items bottom to top while keeping the main axis vertical.
row, so items flow horizontally by default.
nowrap, so items stay on one line and shrink to fit.
flex-start, so items pack toward the start of the main axis.
stretch, so items fill the cross axis of their line.
stretch, so wrapped lines fill the cross axis.
It sizes the item based on its content, similar to max-content.

interview.q: What is the difference between width and flex-basis?
interview.answer: width is a fixed size; flex-basis is the starting size before flex distribution and can be overridden by flex-grow.

interview.q: What happens when flex items overflow?
interview.answer: They overflow the container unless flex-wrap or flex-shrink allows them to fit.

interview.q: How do you make a flex item not shrink?
interview.answer: Set flex-shrink: 0, so it keeps its basis even when space is tight.

interview.q: How do you make a flex item not grow?
interview.answer: Set flex-grow: 0, so it does not absorb free space.

interview.q: What is a flex container's main size?
interview.answer: Its width in row direction or height in column direction, depending on flex-direction.

interview.q: What is a flex item's cross size?
interview.answer: Its height in row direction or width in column direction.
It aligns items by their text baselines, useful for mixed font sizes.

interview.q: What is the difference between baseline and center alignment?
interview.answer: baseline aligns text; center aligns the box midpoints, which can misalign text.
It centres items along the main axis with equal space on both sides.

interview.q: What does justify-items do in flexbox?
interview.answer: Nothing; justify-items is a grid property, not a flexbox property.
A shorthand for align-content and justify-content in grid and flexbox.
A shorthand for align-items and justify-items, mainly used in grid.
A shorthand for align-self and justify-self on a single grid item.

interview.q: How do you vertically centre with flexbox?
interview.answer: Set display: flex, align-items: center and justify-content: center on the container.

interview.q: What is the difference between a flex item and a flex container?
interview.answer: A flex item is a child of a flex container; a flex container is the parent with display: flex.
